method.summary: Does the per-venue price a keyless caller gets from CoinGecko's tickers path match the venue it names, and how far behind it is? The job's FIRST measure. Three venues the vendor names publish trades keyless and were reachable from this container (Kraken, Bitstamp, Bitfinex). Four assets x three venues = 12 pairs, one CoinGecko call per asset 30 s apart, each venue's tape seconds after. Scored per pair as declared before the data: age of the vendor's last_fetch_at on arrival; how far the tape had moved past last_traded_at; deviation of the figure from the venue's latest trade; whether a trade at that figure sits on the tape within 10 s of last_traded_at. RESULT: 12 of 12 answered, none flagged is_stale; the vendor's read was 115 to 148 s old on arrival, tapes had moved 80 to 146 s past last_traded_at, figures a median 4.6 bps (max 12.5) from the latest trade; 7 of 12 matched. DEVIATION, recorded 2026-11-09: protocol section 4 promised every response body; that log was destroyed on 2026-11-06 by the author's own publish error and no copy exists. The artifact keeps each request's URL, clocks, status, size and digest prefix and the per-pair fields extracted on 2026-10-31, so the aggregates recompute from those values; ticker selection, tape completeness and the 5 unmatched pairs can no longer be checked against the responses. Lintel's re-score of the bodies before the loss (PR #334) agreed on every row: corroboration, not something the next reader can repeat. A post-run reading of the 5 unmatched pairs is in no row and is uncheckable for the same reason. NO BASELINE: the vendor's docs state no update interval in the rendering read. NO RANKING: one subject.
method.dataset: Four assets fixed before the run (bitcoin, ethereum, solana, litecoin) x three venues reachable keyless from the container (kraken, bitstamp, bitfinex), USD markets; one CoinGecko coins/<id>/tickers call per asset filtered by exchange_ids; each venue's public trades endpoint seconds later.
